questions.subject: Science
questions.question: February challenge: During pre-board application practice, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Matter in Our Surroundings. which statement best describes diffusion in gases?

options.A: Particles move from higher to lower concentration due to random motion
options.B: Gas particles stop moving at room temperature

questions.explanation: Gas particles move randomly and spread from a region of higher concentration to lower concentration.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: February challenge: During pre-board application practice, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Matter in Our Surroundings. during melting, the temperature of pure ice at its melting point remains constant because the supplied heat is used to:
questions.explanation: Latent heat is used to change the state by overcoming intermolecular attraction.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: February challenge: During pre-board application practice, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Is Matter Around Us Pure. which method is most suitable for separating cream from milk?
questions.explanation: Centrifugation separates components of a mixture based on density.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: February challenge: During pre-board application practice, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Is Matter Around Us Pure. a solution contains 20 g salt in 180 g water. What is its mass percentage of salt?

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: February challenge: During pre-board application practice, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Atoms and Molecules. what is the chemical formula of aluminium oxide?
questions.explanation: Aluminium has valency 3 and oxygen has valency 2; criss-crossing gives Al2O3.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: February challenge: During pre-board application practice, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Atoms and Molecules. how many molecules are present in 18 g of water?
questions.explanation: 18 g water is one mole, containing Avogadro’s number of molecules.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: February challenge: During pre-board application practice, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Structure of the Atom. which subatomic particle has no electric charge?

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: February challenge: During pre-board application practice, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Structure of the Atom. an atom has atomic number 17 and mass number 35. Number of neutrons is:

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: February challenge: During pre-board application practice, a Class 9 learner is reviewing The Fundamental Unit of Life. which cell organelle is the main site of aerobic respiration?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria release usable energy through aerobic cellular respiration.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: February challenge: During pre-board application practice, a Class 9 learner is reviewing The Fundamental Unit of Life. a plant cell placed in a concentrated salt solution shrinks away from its cell wall. This is:
questions.explanation: Water leaves the cell by osmosis, causing the protoplast to shrink.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: February challenge: During pre-board application practice, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Tissues. which plant tissue transports water and minerals from roots?
questions.explanation: Xylem conducts water and dissolved minerals, mainly upward.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: February challenge: During pre-board application practice, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Tissues. which feature makes cardiac muscle suitable for continuous rhythmic activity?
questions.explanation: Intercalated discs connect cardiac cells and support coordinated contraction.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: February challenge: During pre-board application practice, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Motion. the slope of a distance-time graph represents:
questions.explanation: Distance travelled per unit time is speed; it is the graph’s slope.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: February challenge: During pre-board application practice, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Force and Laws of Motion. a 2 kg object accelerates at 3 m/s². The net force is:
questions.explanation: Newton’s second law: F = ma = 2 × 3 = 6 N.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: February challenge: During pre-board application practice, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Gravitation. if the distance between two masses is doubled, their gravitational force becomes:
questions.explanation: Gravitational force varies inversely with the square of distance.
